project.name: automation-api
project.description:
Service-to-service contract for the automation capability (V9 §18 / §91).
Members: EmailReminderPort and ContentPlanPort (the ports), plus the read models and write drafts they carry (EmailReminderView / EmailReminderDraft / ContentPlanView / ContentPlanDraft / ContentPlanEdit).
Why the module exists. Six agent tools reached straight into automation's application layer: EmailReminderTool / QueryEmailRemindersTool / UpdateEmailReminderTool injected EmailReminderService, and QueryPlansTool / SchedulePlanTool / UpdatePlanTool injected BlogContentPlanService. Six implementation statements pointing agent -> automation, all crossing the dinqor-agent / dinqor-content-automation deployment-unit boundary. After the split the agent service could not be built without automation's implementation classes, and every tool was coupled to the exact method list of a concrete @Service -- including its @Value config surface and its mapper.
Direction. Here the *consumer* is agent (it asks for reminders and plans) and the *provider* is automation. So the ports are consumer-shaped: each answers only the questions the six tools actually ask. The three plan tools want six operations (list / create / findByIdempotencyKey / updateStatus / update / delete) and the three reminder tools want five plus the two status constants -- not the twenty-odd public methods those two services expose to their own controllers.
Why the DTOs are NARROWED, not mirrored, unlike ContentPost. The mirror rule (docs/migration/adr-contract-boundaries.md §2.5) exists for a type that *replaces* a frontend-visible one: mirroring then makes "serialization is byte-identical" a provable statement, which is what keeps the cut a pure refactor. None of these types replaces anything. automation.api.EmailReminderTaskVO and BlogContentPlanVO stay exactly where they are and keep going to the frontend unchanged from automation.api.EmailReminderController / BlogContentPlanController. The contract types are new, on a new seam, and the frontend never sees them. They therefore carry exactly the fields the tools read, and every field has a named consumer. Mirroring would have copied 24 fields of BlogContentPlanVO -- including four runs of adjacent same-typed components, which is a position-order hazard with no compile-time protection -- to preserve a serialization surface that does not exist. What IS pinned is the component order, by reflection, and the tool output JSON, by the tools' own tests.
Why jakarta.validation annotations are NOT here. automation.api.EmailReminderCreateRequest and BlogContentPlanCreateRequest carry @NotBlank / @Pattern / @Size / @Email / @Min / @Max. Those are the HTTP boundary's business: they fire because the controller annotates the parameter @Valid. A contract may not carry them anyway (they would add a dependency, and ADR-1 keeps this module framework-free). Nothing is lost on the agent path, which never had them: the tools build their arguments from JSON and validate by hand before calling. The domain-side request types keep their annotations and stay the validated front door for the HTTP callers.
Package note: this module's package is com.xander.lab.automation.spi, NOT com.xander.lab.automation.api. automation already owns com.xander.lab.automation.api as its *frontend HTTP* layer -- 20 files of controllers, VOs and request bodies. Declaring the contract there would put one package in two jars, and would make the scanner classify those controllers as shared kernel, turning "a controller imports its own application layer" into dozens of automation.api -> automation backlog edges plus a shared-kernel-reverse-dependency violation each. Same collision as agent-api and studio-api; same answer. SHARED_KERNEL lists automation.spi (dotted, matched longest-first, so it does not swallow automation.application).
What is deliberately NOT here yet: - Any of automation's own api layer (com.xander.lab.automation.api.*). It is the frontend HTTP contract, a different audience, and it joins a contract module only when that layer itself is split in Wave 2. - The BlogNotificationService port that knowledgebase needs, and the SSE broadcast port that admin needs. Both belong here (same capability, same direction) and both are zero-wiring extensions of this module; they are simply not part of this cut. - The email-reminder mail template. integration.mail.MailService imports automation.domain.EmailReminderMailTemplates, which is the reverse direction and closes a real automation <-> integration cycle: automation's EmailReminderScheduler calls MailService#sendReminderMail, which calls back into automation to render the body. Breaking that cycle is a separate cut because it changes MailService's API, and it is recorded in docs/migration/lib-extraction.md.
Zero dependencies, and that is the point. A contract that drags in a framework cannot be depended on by every service, and V9 §19 is explicit that the WebFlux Gateway must stay free of spring-webmvc. Nothing here may gain a compile dependency without a deliberate decision; test scope is fine.
